claim: Advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is associated with a poor prognosis.
source: Advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is associated with a poor prognosis, and biomarkers that predict response to treatment are highly desirable.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract and introduction without specific data provided in this manuscript.

claim: The baseline risk signature has three covariates and was strongly driven by baseline percentage of CD33+CD14+HLADRhigh monocytes.
source: The baseline risk signature has three covariates and was strongly driven by baseline percentage of CD33 + CD14 + HLADR high monocytes.
evidence: This claim is supported by the Bayesian multivariate regression analysis results presented in Figure 2B showing the three covariates.

claim: The combined signature has six covariates, also featuring baseline CD33+CD14+HLADRhigh monocytes but is strongly driven by on-treatment relative change of CD8+ central memory T cells percentages.
source: The combined signature has six covariates, also featuring baseline CD33 + CD14 + HLADR high monocytes but is strongly driven by on-treatment relative change of CD8 + central memory T cells percentages.
evidence: This is supported by the proportional hazards regression analysis results shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: The combined model has a higher predictive power than the baseline model.
source: The combined model has a higher predictive power than the baseline model and was successfully validated to predict therapeutic response in an independent cohort of nine patients from an additional Phase 2 trial (NCT03494322)
evidence: The combined risk scores exhibited a stronger correlation with PFS than the baseline risk scores (C-index=0.69, τ=−0.49, p=7e-7) compared to baseline (C-index=0.60, τ=−0.33, p=0.0005).

claim: The combined model was successfully validated to predict therapeutic response in an independent cohort of nine patients from the EACH trial (NCT03494322).
source: The combined model has a higher predictive power than the baseline model and was successfully validated to predict therapeutic response in an independent cohort of nine patients from an additional Phase 2 trial (NCT03494322) assessing the addition of avelumab to cetuximab treatment in HNSCC.
evidence: The combined risk signature strongly correlated with a poorer treatment outcome (τ=0.73, p=0.02) in the validation cohort as shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Tissue counterparts for the immune cells driving the models specifically colocalized at the tissue level and correlated with outcome.
source: We identified tissue counterparts for the immune cells driving the models, using imaging mass cytometry, that specifically colocalized at the tissue level and correlated with outcome.
evidence: Imaging mass cytometry analysis showed that CD8Trm cells were significantly more likely to be in contact with CD74+ macrophages (Figure 6E), and these populations correlated with PFS.

claim: Eighty-seven patients were enrolled in the clinical trial NCT02633800.
source: Eighty-seven patients were enrolled in the clinical trial.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the study design and enrollment.

claim: Thirty-one patients were excluded due to incomplete paired biological datasets, leaving 56 patients for analysis.
source: Thirty-one patients were excluded due to incomplete paired biological datasets, leaving 56 patients for analysis.
evidence: This describes the final analysis cohort after exclusions.

claim: There was no difference in PFS between patients who received patritumab and those who did not.
source: Amongst these patients, there was no difference in PFS as demonstrated by Kaplan-Meier survival curve analysis (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) regardless of whether the patients received patritumab, which reflected the results published in the clinical trial.
evidence: Kaplan-Meier survival curve analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 demonstrates no difference in PFS.

claim: The baseline clinical characteristics did not significantly differ between the placebo and patritumab cohorts.
source: The baseline clinical characteristics, as well as value of the laboratory-based covariates at baseline and after one cycle of treatment, did not significantly differ between the placebo and patritumab cohorts (Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is supported by data presented in Supplementary file 3.

claim: Baseline CD33+CD14+ monocytes have a β value of –1.05 and are predictive of better PFS.
source: Evaluation of the individual β values reveal that baseline CD33+CD14+ monocytes and DN B cells have a β value of –1.05 and –0.53, respectively, and hence a higher baseline value of both populations is predictive of better PFS.
evidence: This is derived from the Bayesian multivariate proportional hazards regression analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Double negative B cells have a β value of –0.53 and are predictive of better PFS.
source: Evaluation of the individual β values reveal that baseline CD33+CD14+ monocytes and DN B cells have a β value of –1.05 and –0.53, respectively, and hence a higher baseline value of both populations is predictive of better PFS.
evidence: This is derived from the Bayesian multivariate proportional hazards regression analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Age has a β value of 0.47 and is associated with poorer PFS.
source: Age, with a β value of 0.47, is associated with poorer PFS.
evidence: This is derived from the Bayesian multivariate proportional hazards regression analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The baseline risk scores correlated strongly with PFS (C-index=0.60, τ=−0.33, p=0.0005).
source: The baseline risk scores correlated strongly with PFS (C-index=0.60, τ=−0.33, p=0.0005).
evidence: Statistical analysis of the baseline risk signature performance.

claim: The median PFS of the low-risk and high-risk cohorts in the baseline model are 8.3 and 3.6 months, respectively (log rank p-value = 6.0e-5).
source: The median PFS of the low-risk and high-risk cohorts are 8.3 and 3.6 months, respectively (log rank p-value = 6.0e-5).
evidence: This is shown in the Kaplan-Meier curve in Figure 2D.

claim: Baseline CD4+ memory regulatory T cells (HLA-DR-CD45RO+Tregs) are associated with better survival in the combined model.
source: A total of six covariates were identified – three immune subpopulations with negative β values and hence associated with better survival, that is, baseline CD33+CD14+ monocytes, baseline CD4+ memory regulatory T cells (HLA-DR-CD45RO+Tregs), and an increase in CD8+ effector memory T cells (CD45RO+CCR7-).
evidence: This is derived from the proportional hazards regression analysis shown in Figure 3A.

claim: An increase in CD8+ effector memory T cells (CD45RO+CCR7-) is associated with better survival in the combined model.
source: A total of six covariates were identified – three immune subpopulations with negative β values and hence associated with better survival, that is, baseline CD33+CD14+ monocytes, baseline CD4+ memory regulatory T cells (HLA-DR-CD45RO+Tregs), and an increase in CD8+ effector memory T cells (CD45RO+CCR7-).
evidence: This is derived from the proportional hazards regression analysis shown in Figure 3A.

claim: An increase in CD8+ central memory T cells (CD45RO+CCR7+) is associated with inferior PFS.
source: An increase in two subpopulations, CD8+ central memory T cells (CD45RO+CCR7+) and CD3 T cells, was associated with inferior PFS.
evidence: This is derived from the proportional hazards regression analysis shown in Figure 3A.

claim: An increase in CD3 T cells is associated with inferior PFS.
source: An increase in two subpopulations, CD8+ central memory T cells (CD45RO+CCR7+) and CD3 T cells, was associated with inferior PFS.
evidence: This is derived from the proportional hazards regression analysis shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The hypopharyngeal primary tumour site is associated with poorer PFS.
source: The hypopharyngeal primary tumour site was also associated with a poorer PFS (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This is shown in the proportional hazards regression analysis in Figure 3A and B.

claim: The combined risk scores exhibited a stronger correlation with PFS than the baseline risk scores (C-index=0.69, τ=−0.49, p=7e-7).
source: The combined risk scores exhibited a stronger correlation with PFS than the baseline risk scores (C-index=0.69, τ=−0.49, p=7e-7).
evidence: Statistical analysis comparing the combined and baseline models.

claim: The median PFS of the low-risk and high-risk cohorts in the combined model are 6.8 and 3.6 months, respectively (log rank p-value 0.004).
source: In this combined predictive signature, the median PFS of the low-risk and high-risk cohorts are 6.8 and 3.6 months, respectively (log rank p-value 0.004) (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is shown in the Kaplan-Meier curve in Figure 3C.

claim: The difference in EGFR-ErbB3 FRET (FRET.delta) was associated with a negative β value suggesting better PFS.
source: In Figure 3A (fourth covariate from the bottom), the difference in EGFR-ErbB3 FRET (FRET.delta) was associated with a negative β value which suggests a better PFS.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3A but did not meet the stringent criteria for inclusion in the final signature.

claim: A significant correlation was identified between the log fold changes of miR-21-5p with the corresponding log fold changes of CD33+CD14+ monocytes (r=0.43, p=0.02).
source: By correlating the miRNA changes in our study with this monocytic subpopulation, a significant correlation was identified between the log fold changes of miR-21-5p with the corresponding log fold changes of CD33+CD14+ monocytes (r=0.43, p=0.02, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This correlation is shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Patient PFS data strongly and inversely correlated with best objective response (BOR) (τ=−0.52, p=3e-6).
source: We confirmed that in the original test cohort, patient PFS data strongly and inversely correlated with BOR (τ=−0.52, p=3e-6) (Figure 5A).
evidence: This correlation is shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The combined risk signature strongly correlated with a poorer treatment outcome in the validation cohort (τ=0.73, p=0.02).
source: The combined risk signature strongly correlated with a poorer treatment outcome (τ=0.73, p=0.02) (Figure 5B).
evidence: This validation result is shown in Figure 5B.

claim: High pre-treatment levels of CD33+CD14+ monocytes significantly correlated with a worse disease outcome in the validation cohort.
source: High pre-treatment levels of CD33+CD14+monocytes significantly correlated with a worse disease outcome in all patients except for a single outlier who exhibited a complete response to treatment.
evidence: This is described in the validation cohort analysis section.

claim: A post-treatment increase in CD8+ central memory cells (lfcCD8CM) correlated with a poorer treatment outcome in the validation cohort.
source: A post-treatment increase in CD8+ central memory cells (lfcCD8CM) also correlated with a poorer treatment outcome.
evidence: This is described in the validation cohort analysis section.

claim: Baseline CD33+CD14+ monocytes modestly predicted PFS as a univariate (log rank p-value = 0.03).
source: We observed a modest split that reached significance only in the case of baseline CD33+CD14+ monocyte (log rank p-value = 0.03) and not in the case of lfcCD8CM cells (log rank p-value = 0.1).
evidence: This is shown in the Kaplan-Meier curves in Figure 5C.

claim: lfcCD8CM more strongly predicted PFS (C-index=0.74, τ=−0.36, p=0.01) than baseline CD33+CD14+ monocytes (C-index=0.39, τ=0.22, p=0.07).
source: lfcCD8CM more strongly predicted PFS (C-index=0.74, τ=−0.36, p=0.01) than base line CD33+CD14+ monocytes (C-index=0.39, τ=0.22, p=0.07).
evidence: Statistical comparison of univariate predictive power.

claim: CD14+CD16+CD33+CD11b+ monocytes also express high levels of HLA-DR.
source: Due to the consistency with which the CD33+CD14+ monocyte population appeared across our study, we wanted to further characterize this population to determine its phenotype hence we expanded the antibody panel for the validation set and determined that these CD14+CD16+CD33+CD11b+ monocytes also express high levels of HLA-DR (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This characterization is shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claim: The peripheral intermediate monocyte population strongly correlated with a tissue CD14+CD33+CD74+CD68+ macrophage population.
source: The peripheral intermediate monocyte population strongly correlated with a tissue CD14+CD33+CD74+CD68+ macrophage population while the CD8CM inversely correlated with CD45RO+CD27+CD8+ tissue resident memory T cell (CD8Trm) population.
evidence: This correlation is described in the imaging mass cytometry analysis section and shown in Figure 6D.

claim: CD8CM inversely correlated with CD45RO+CD27+CD8+ tissue resident memory T cell (CD8Trm) population.
source: The peripheral intermediate monocyte population strongly correlated with a tissue CD14+CD33+CD74+CD68+ macrophage population while the CD8CM inversely correlated with CD45RO+CD27+CD8+ tissue resident memory T cell (CD8Trm) population.
evidence: This correlation is described in the imaging mass cytometry analysis section and shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Both CD14+CD33+CD74+CD68+ macrophages and CD8Trm populations positively correlated with PFS.
source: Both of those populations positively correlated with PFS.
evidence: This is stated in the imaging mass cytometry results section.

claim: The peripheral CD33+ monocyte population strongly correlated with CD8Trm.
source: Interestingly, the peripheral CD33+ monocyte population strongly correlated with CD8Trm (Figure 6D).
evidence: This correlation is shown in Figure 6D.

claim: CD8Trm cells were significantly more likely to be in contact with a CD74+ macrophage than any other identified population.
source: We found these cells were significantly more likely to be in contact with a CD74+ macrophage than any other identified population suggesting this interaction is biologically driven and not random (Figure 6E).
evidence: This cell-to-cell contact analysis is shown in Figure 6E.

claim: The EXTREME regimen, consisting of platinum-based chemotherapy and cetuximab, was the standard-of-care first-line systemic treatment for recurrent or metastatic HNSCC for many years.
source: For many years, the standard-of-care first-line systemic treatment was the EXTREME regimen, consisting of a platinum-based chemotherapy regimen and cetuximab, an anti-EGFR monoclonal antibody (Van Cutsem et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Van Cutsem et al., 2009.

claim: The KEYNOTE-048 trial in 2019 changed the treatment paradigm for R/M HNSCC patients by incorporating pembrolizumab into the first-line setting.
source: The KEYNOTE-048 trial in 2019 changed the treatment paradigm for these patients by incorporating pembrolizumab, an immune checkpoint inhibitor, into the first-line setting (Burtness et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Burtness et al., 2019.

claim: The EXTREME regimen remains a first-line standard-of-care for patients with PD-L1 negative tumours or those with contraindications to anti-PD1 immunotherapy.
source: However, the EXTREME regimen remains a first-line standard-of-care for a substantial number of patients, specifically those with programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1) negative tumours or those with contraindications to the use of anti-PD1 immunotherapy.
evidence: This is stated as current clinical practice knowledge.

claim: miR-21-5p and miR-142-3p have previously demonstrated prognostic and predictive utility in HNSCC.
source: We also incorporated the analysis of two circulating microRNAs (miRNAs) from exosomes: miR-21-5p and miR-142-3p, which have previously demonstrated prognostic and predictive utility (Summerer et al., 2015; Vahabi et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Summerer et al., 2015 and Vahabi et al., 2021.

claim: The 5-year relative survival of patients with hypopharyngeal SCC is consistently the worst amongst different anatomical HNSCC sub-sites.
source: This corroborates previous findings that the 5-year relative survival of patients with hypopharyngeal SCC is consistently the worst amongst different anatomical HNSCC sub-sites (Gatta et al., 2017; Machiels et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Gatta et al., 2017 and Machiels et al., 2020.

claim: Hypopharyngeal tumours have a propensity to present at the de novo advanced stage.
source: The propensity of hypopharyngeal tumours to present at the de novo advanced stage (Cadoni et al., 2017) and the density of submucosal lymphatics in this anatomical region translates into these patients inherently performing worse
evidence: This is supported by citation to Cadoni et al., 2017.

claim: The addition of patritumab did not produce any benefit to PFS in the Phase 2 clinical trial.
source: The notable absence of patritumab (denoted as 'Drug') in our predictive signatures is also consistent with the outcome of the Phase 2 clinical trial where the addition of this investigational medicinal product did not produce any benefit to PFS (Forster et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Forster et al., 2019 and the trial results.

claim: There is a high level of inter-individual heterogeneity in the relative abundance of PBMC subpopulations even between healthy donors.
source: There is a high level of inter-individual heterogeneity in the relative abundance of PBMC subpopulations even between healthy donors.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the discussion.

claim: Intermediate monocytes have a key role in antigen presentation.
source: This monocyte population matches the population of intermediate monocytes described in the literature shown to have a key role in antigen presentation (Cravens et al., 2007; Zawada et al., 2011; Wong et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cravens et al., 2007; Zawada et al., 2011; Wong et al., 2011.

claim: Cetuximab treatment can increase TCR diversity in peripheral T cells.
source: Indeed, cetuximab treatment can be a source of tumour-derived antigens as it has been shown to increase TCR diversity in peripheral T cells as well as cross-presentation by antigen-presenting cells (Kansy et al., 2018; Srivastava et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kansy et al., 2018 and Srivastava et al., 2013.

claim: Cetuximab treatment can increase cross-presentation by antigen-presenting cells.
source: Indeed, cetuximab treatment can be a source of tumour-derived antigens as it has been shown to increase TCR diversity in peripheral T cells as well as cross-presentation by antigen-presenting cells (Kansy et al., 2018; Srivastava et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kansy et al., 2018 and Srivastava et al., 2013.

claim: Monocyte-derived macrophages have been shown to activate and expand tissue resident memory T cells.
source: Nevertheless, monocyte-derived macrophages have been shown to activate and expand tissue resident memory T cells (Trm) (Snyder et al., 2021; Low et al., 2020; Muntjewerff et al., 2020; Chu et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Snyder et al., 2021; Low et al., 2020; Muntjewerff et al., 2020; Chu et al., 2020.

claim: High levels of pre-treatment CD8CM cells correlating with a favourable treatment outcome in HNSCC has been previously reported by the Whiteside group.
source: Interestingly, high levels of pre-treatment CD8CM cells correlating with a favourable treatment outcome in HNSCC has been previously and independently reported by the Whiteside group indirectly validating our results (Czystowska et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Czystowska et al., 2013.

claim: Tumour reactive T cell clones can be found in the periphery.
source: Using single-cell sequencing and mapping of T cell receptor clonality at the levels of TILs and peripheral T cells, researchers have definitively proven that tumour reactive T cell clones can be found in the periphery (Fairfax et al., 2020; Kok et al., 2020; Pauken et al., 2021; Padrón et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Fairfax et al., 2020; Kok et al., 2020; Pauken et al., 2021; Padrón et al., 2022.

claim: There is continuous recruitment of memory T cells from the periphery into the tumour which replenishes the pool of tissue Trm.
source: The movement of these cells between the tumour and draining lymph node was recently investigated using photoactivable T cells in mice which showed that there is continuous recruitment of memory T cells from the periphery into the tumour which replenishes the pool of tissue Trm identified by CD103 and TCF1 expression.
evidence: This is based on recent research cited in the discussion.

claim: CD8CM are capable of homing into inflamed tissue and undergoing transcriptional reprogramming to a stable Trm phenotype.
source: The peripheral origin of Trm cells is still under investigation with recent data suggesting that CD8CM are not only capable of homing into the inflamed tissue but also undergoing transcriptional reprogramming to a stable Trm phenotype (Matos et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Matos et al., 2022.

claim: Trm has been identified as a key player in anti-tumour immunity in HNSCC and other cancers.
source: We hypothesize that the predictive power of the population of peripheral CD8CM stems from its ability to home to the tumour and contribute to the Trm population which has recently been identified as key player in anti-tumour immunity in HNSCC as well as other cancers mainly in the context of immunotherapy but also in chemo/radiotherapy (Han et al., 2021; Ida et al., 2021; Savas et al., 2018; Djenidi et al., 2015; Luoma et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Han et al., 2021; Ida et al., 2021; Savas et al., 2018; Djenidi et al., 2015; Luoma et al., 2022.

claim: A multimodal analysis taking into account both clinicopathological and laboratory-based biological covariates at different timepoints would provide better predictive value than single modality approaches.
source: We hypothesize that a multimodal analysis, taking into account both clinicopathological and laboratory-based biological covariates at different timepoints, would provide better predictive value.
evidence: This hypothesis is tested and supported by the superior performance of the combined model over the baseline model.

claim: The detailed definition of a broad immune cell signature could contribute to the development of assays employing liquid biopsies to predict clinical outcomes.
source: We hypothesized that the detailed definition of a broad immune cell signature could contribute to the development of assays employing liquid biopsies to predict clinical outcomes.
evidence: This hypothesis is supported by the successful development and validation of the risk signature.

claim: CD33+CD14+CD16+HLADRhigh monocytes represent the same group of cells as CD14+CD33+CD74+CD68+ tissue macrophages that gain CD68 expression as they enter the tissue.
source: Myeloid cells are plastic yet given the similarity in the marker expression patterns between the peripheral CD33+CD14+CD16+HLADRhigh monocyte population and the CD14+CD33+CD74+CD68+ tissue macrophages, as well as the strong correlation between their corresponding blood and tissue abundance (Figure 6D), we hypothesize that they represent the same group of cells that gain CD68 expression as they enter the tissue.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on marker similarity and correlation data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: The myeloid population may have a role in inducing post-treatment expansion of CD8CM potentially via cross-presentation of antigens released by drug-induced cancer cell death.
source: Given the correlation between tissue levels CD8+ memory T cell, peripheral intermediate monocytes, and the tissue colocalization of the CD8+ memory T cells with the CD74+ macrophages, we can imagine a role for our myeloid population in inducing post-treatment expansion of CD8CM potentially via a mechanism involving cross-presentation of antigens released by drug-induced cancer cell death (Colbert et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on observed correlations and colocalization, supported by citation to Colbert et al., 2020.

claim: The predictive power of peripheral CD8CM stems from its ability to home to the tumour and contribute to the Trm population.
source: We hypothesize that the predictive power of the population of peripheral CD8CM stems from its ability to home to the tumour and contribute to the Trm population
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the observed inverse correlation between peripheral CD8CM and tissue Trm, and literature on T cell trafficking.

claim: The accumulation of clonally expanded memory T cells in the periphery in poor responders is the potential result of tumour-induced T cell exclusion.
source: The accumulation of clonally expanded memory T cells in the periphery in poor responders is the potential result of tumour-induced T cell exclusion which we can infer from the negative correlation observed between peripheral and tumour infiltrating memory T cells (Jerby-Arnon et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the observed negative correlation and supported by citation to Jerby-Arnon et al., 2018.

claim: In the proposed model, CD8+ memory T cells are being generated only in patients having a large pre-treatment pool of competent APCs yet these anti-tumour CD8+ memory cells cannot enter the tumour from the periphery hence accumulating in circulation.
source: In this model CD8+ memory T cells are being generated only in patients having a large pre-treatment pool of competent APCs yet these anti-tumour CD8+ memory cells cannot enter the tumour from the periphery hence accumulating in circulation.
evidence: This is a mechanistic model proposed to explain the observed data.

claim: Sixteen patients were enrolled in the EACH trial (NCT03494322).
source: Sixteen patients were enrolled in the study.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the validation cohort enrollment.

claim: Four patients in the EACH trial were excluded due to lack of blood samples at both timepoints.
source: Four patients were excluded due to lack of blood samples at both timepoints.
evidence: This describes exclusions from the validation cohort.

claim: One patient in the EACH trial was excluded due to lack of outcome data.
source: One patient was excluded due to lack of outcome data.
evidence: This describes exclusions from the validation cohort.

claim: Two patients in the EACH trial only had a baseline biopsy.
source: Two patients only had a baseline biopsy.
evidence: This describes the sample availability in the validation cohort.

claim: One patient in the EACH trial was excluded due to poor PBMC viability.
source: PBMCs underwent a quality control step to check viability which resulted in the exclusion of one of the patients (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This describes quality control exclusions from the validation cohort.

claim: One patient in the EACH trial died before their first response evaluation scan and was classified as having progressive disease.
source: One patient died before their first response evaluation scan and was therefore classified as having progressive disease as the cause of death was identified to be the illness.
evidence: This describes outcome classification in the validation cohort.

claim: Sufficient tissue for imaging mass cytometry profiling was obtained from nine patients.
source: We obtained sufficient tissue from the biopsy at trial enrolment for in-depth profiling by imaging mass cytometry from nine patients.
evidence: This describes the sample size for the imaging mass cytometry analysis.

claim: None of the superpopulations identified by imaging mass cytometry correlated with PFS.
source: The distribution of the superpopulations per patient is shown in Figure 6B, yet none of which correlated with PFS (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Bayesian multivariate proportional hazards regression was used to rank and select covariates by predictive importance.
source: Using Bayesian multivariate proportional hazards regression, covariates were ranked and selected by predictive importance (Grigoriadis et al., 2018).
evidence: This describes the statistical method used, supported by citation to Grigoriadis et al., 2018.

claim: The relative efficiency of the predictive model was assessed using C-index and rank correlation of the signature-generated risk scores with survival time.
source: The relative efficiency of the predictive model was assessed by using C-index (a metric proposed by Harrell et al., 1984, to evaluate the accuracy of predictions made by an algorithm) and rank correlation of the signature-generated risk scores with survival time.
evidence: This describes the evaluation metrics used, with citation to Harrell et al., 1984.

claim: Systematic iterative covariate rejection and cross-validation (5000 iterations) allowed for the selection of an optimal covariate set to avoid overfitting.
source: Systematic iterative covariate rejection and cross-validation (5000 iterations) allowed for the selection of an optimal covariate set to avoid overfitting though inclusion of too many covariates.
evidence: This describes the statistical methodology used.

claim: Exosomes were prepared using an optimized centrifugation method.
source: Exosomes were prepared using an optimized centrifugation method (Monypenny et al., 2018).
evidence: This describes the experimental method, supported by citation to Monypenny et al., 2018.

claim: Normalization of RNA between cycle 1 and cycle 2 therapy was performed using the expression levels of the housekeeping gene 18S.
source: Normalization of the RNA, between cycle 1 and cycle 2 therapy of each patient, was performed using the expression levels of the housekeeping gene 18S (Assay ID, Hs99999901_s1).
evidence: This describes the experimental normalization method.

claim: Quantification of gene expression in circulating exosomes was performed by droplet digital PCR.
source: Quantification of gene expression in circulating exosomes was performed by droplet digital polymerase chain reaction (ddPCR) (Bio-Rad QX100 system).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used.

claim: Exosomes were imaged on an 'Open' fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) system.
source: Exosomes were imaged on an 'Open' fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) system (Barber et al., 2013).
evidence: This describes the imaging method, supported by citation to Barber et al., 2013.

claim: Analysis of FLIM data was performed with the TRI2 software.
source: Analysis was performed with the TRI2 software (v2.7.8.9, CRUK/MRC Oxford Institute for Radiation Oncology, Oxford) as described previously (Barber et al., 2009; Rowley et al., 2016).
evidence: This describes the analysis software, supported by citations to Barber et al., 2009 and Rowley et al., 2016.

claim: Imaging analysis was performed using R packages including RandomForest for classification and regression, and Raster and SF for image manipulation and segmentation.
source: Imaging analysis was performed using the following R packages: RandomForest for classification and regression, Raster and SF for image manipulation and segmentation.
evidence: This describes the computational analysis methods.

claim: Written informed consent was obtained from all patients in both trials.
source: Written informed consent was obtained. Approval was obtained from ethics committees (Research Ethics Committee reference: 15/LO/1670). ... Written informed consent was obtained from all patients. Study approval was obtained from ethics committees (Research Ethics Committee reference: 18/LO/0021).
evidence: This describes the ethical approval and consent process.

claim: The risk signature can serve as a non-invasive risk stratification for patients with R/M HNSCC using only peripheral blood.
source: This risk signature can serve as a non-invasive risk stratification for patients with R/M HNSCC using only peripheral blood, guiding the clinician toward the likelihood of success early during the treatment course.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the study findings.

claim: The immune-based combined multimodality signature presents a novel means of predicting response early on during the treatment course.
source: This immune-based combined multimodality signature, obtained through longitudinal peripheral blood monitoring and validated in an independent cohort, presents a novel means of predicting response early on during the treatment course.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the abstract based on the study findings.
